clue.text: Fuel reserves first found just beneath the surface

indicators.note: first places the reserves ahead of the fuel in the answer

parts.note: reserves on a team bench are subs
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Oil reserves discovered only just below ground level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuel reserves' reads as one phrase about oil stocks, but the reserves are SUBS and 'first' puts them ahead of OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsoil is the layer of earth lying immediately under the topsoil, so it is what is found just below ground.

clue.text: Adjust place where 2, say, sits on board

definitions.meaning: to adjust or settle, as in squaring things up

definitions.text: place where 2, say, sits on board
definitions.meaning: a bishop, the answer to 2, stands on one of the cells of a chessboard

explanation.definitionFit: To square something is to adjust it; and a chess piece such as a bishop occupies a cell of the board.

clue.text: Clergyman twice seen at dance

parts.note: bis is Latin for twice, used in music for a repeat
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A churchman spotted at a dance on two occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: BIS, meaning twice or encore, is a convention a solver may not know; 'seen at' simply joins it to HOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is a senior member of the clergy, so clergyman is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Set bonuses distributed with insensitivity

indicators.note: distributed suggests the letters being shared out and spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Handing out fixed bonuses in a tactless way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges the ten letters of SET BONUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuseness is dullness of perception, a lack of sensitivity to what others feel.

clue.text: Undesirable person first to be taken in by wind-up

indicators.note: to be taken in by means the next piece sits inside the one that follows it
up in a down clue says the word for wind is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to reel is to wind, as a fishing line

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word person

explanation.surface: An unwanted individual who is fooled by a practical joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undesirable' is a noun here (an outcast). 'up' turns REEL into LEER, and 'to be taken in by' puts P (first of 'person') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A leper is figuratively a social outcast, someone shunned by others as undesirable.

clue.text: Penny all but broke can opener

indicators.note: broke suggests the words all but are smashed and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Someone nearly penniless trying to open a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but' looks like 'almost', but it is the fodder: 'broke' rearranges ALLBUT into ULLTAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A pull tab is the ring on a drinks can that you pull to open it, literally the opener of a can.

clue.text: Regularly spray leaders at break in gym

indicators.note: Regularly tells us to take every other letter of the words that follow, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Sports captains periodically hosing things down during a pause at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' picks the even letters across 'spray leaders at break'.
explanation.definitionFit: A palaestra was an ancient Greek wrestling school, a public place for athletic training.

clue.text: Officer returned to cocktail bar

indicators.note: returned in a down clue signals the officer's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Col is short for colonel, an army officer
the tail of the word cock, its last letter

explanation.surface: An officer heading back to the cocktail bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' is read as 'cock tail', the final letter K of COCK; 'returned' turns COL into LOC.
explanation.definitionFit: To lock is to bar, as with a door, so the verb is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Cunning chess player takes castle after start of play

indicators.note: takes means the chess player's name holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: Mikhail Tal was a world chess champion

indicators.note: after sends the castle piece behind the start of the play

parts.note: Act I is the opening of a play
C is taken as an abbreviation for castle

explanation.surface: A crafty chess master captures a rook early in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'castle after start of play' gives ACT I then C, and 'takes' puts that inside TAL, the Latvian world champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactical means cleverly planned for advantage, so it is a synonym for cunning or shrewd.

clue.text: Wally meets sweetheart beside a line in California

parts.note: a wally and a berk are both British slang for a fool
the heart of sweet is its central letter, the E
a ley is a line, as in ley lines joining ancient sites

explanation.surface: A fool meets their beloved next to a queue in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is split as 'sweet heart', the middle E of SWEET. BERK and WALLY are British slang for an idiot. The city was named after Bishop Berkeley.
explanation.definitionFit: Berkeley is a university city in California, on San Francisco Bay.

clue.text: Members of group settle complaint

indicators.note: Members of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Club members resolve a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members of' points to letters inside 'group settle'.
explanation.definitionFit: An upset, as in an upset stomach, is a minor illness or ailment, which is one sense of complaint.

clue.text: Force vehicle off polar ice with clubs

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are gone wrong and need resetting

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A vehicle driving off the polar ice cap carrying golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges POLARICE with C (clubs).
explanation.definitionFit: The police force uses a patrol car, so a force vehicle is a police car.

clue.text: Back entrance to show site of church division

indicators.note: Back says the word for entrance is read the other way round

parts.note: a door is an entrance
to screen is to show, as a film

explanation.surface: Showing a film at the rear entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns DOOR into ROOD; 'to' joins it to SCREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood screen is the carved partition separating nave from chancel, the point where a church is divided.

clue.text: English bank

definitions.meaning: in billiards and snooker, English (US) or ... is spin put on the ball
the bank of a river is its edge

explanation.definitionFit: Side is the British term for spin on a cue ball (called English in America), and a riverside is a bank.

clue.text: Depression sure to develop after hip contracts

indicators.note: after puts the depression behind the word for hip

parts.note: hip, meaning fashionable, is in
a dent is a small depression

indicators.note: to develop suggests the letters of sure growing into a new shape

explanation.surface: A dip that is sure to appear after a hip operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hip' looks anatomical, but it is the slang for fashionable; the plural definition 'contracts' is a noun, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Indentures are formal contracts, especially those binding an apprentice to a master.

clue.text: Quiet evening's a big blow for singer in 8 1 down

parts.note: a quiet evening at home is a night in
a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: A peaceful evening is spoilt by a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the song 'A Nightingale Sang in Berkeley Square'; Berkeley Square is in London's Mayfair.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightingale is a songbird, famously the one in the song set in Berkeley Square.

clue.text: Found overturned barrel to be a source of oil

parts.note: to found is to ground, to give a base to

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means the word for barrel is turned upside down

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel

explanation.surface: A barrel knocked over turns out to contain oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns TUN into NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The groundnut, or peanut, is pressed to make cooking oil.

clue.text: Small boy hit in disturbances

indicators.note: in places the blow inside the small boy

parts.note: Les is a boy's name
to cuff is to hit with an open hand

explanation.surface: A little lad struck during some trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boy' is a man's name here, a crossword habit: any short given name may stand for boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuffles are brief confused fights, minor disturbances of the peace.

clue.text: City gent raised little money going topless

indicators.note: raised in a down clue says the man's name is read upwards

parts.note: Rolf is a man's name

indicators.note: going topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: pence are small coins

explanation.surface: A man in the city raised a small sum by going without a shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns ROLF into FLOR; 'going topless' drops the P of PENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is the Tuscan city, capital of Italy's Renaissance art; also Florence Nightingale's birthplace.

clue.text: Drag coolest produce in here?

indicators.note: produce read as a verb tells us to make something new from the letters

explanation.surface: Is this where you would haul the chilliest fruit and vegetables?
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' works twice: as the anagram signal for DRAG COOLEST and as the farm goods the whole clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold storage keeps perishable goods chilled, so it is where cooled produce would be dragged.

clue.text: Offence committed in front of a theatre of 17 14

indicators.note: in front of puts the offence ahead of the letter A

parts.note: a crime is an offence carried out

explanation.surface: A crime committed before a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is thematic: Florence Nightingale nursed in the Crimean War; a 'theatre' of war is its setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimea is the peninsula where the war in which Florence Nightingale nursed was fought, her theatre of action.

clue.text: Weary man born where 8 was 2

parts.note: to cloy is to weary by excess
ne is French for born, used of a man (nee for a woman)

explanation.surface: A tired man was born where the philosopher was a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: George Berkeley, the philosopher, was Bishop of Cloyne in Ireland, the thematic link to 8 and 2.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloyne in County Cork is the Irish diocese of which Berkeley was bishop.

clue.text: 1 down of 2 said to be in front

indicators.note: said tells us the answer is spoken like a number

parts.note: the square of the number 2 is four

explanation.surface: The square in front of the bishop on a chessboard.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 down' (SQUARE) and '2' are read as numbers: two squared is four, and 'said' gives the like-sounding word for forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Fore means at or toward the front, as in foreground or forecourt.

clue.text: Become natural? Lie on one side

indicators.note: Become suggests the letters turning into something else

explanation.surface: A naturist told to lie on their side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Become' rearranges NATURAL with LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unilateral means relating to only one side, from Latin for one side.

clue.text: Scrounger taps general first

indicators.note: first puts the general before the taps

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general
C and H mark the cold and hot taps

explanation.surface: A freeloader drains the general first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taps' means the letters on bath taps, C and H.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech figuratively is a person who sponges off others, a scrounger.

clue.text: A refusal to hold red flower in 17

indicators.note: to hold puts the colour inside the other pieces

parts.note: no is a refusal
R is short for red

explanation.surface: A rejection to keep a red flower in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' is something that flows, a river: the Arno flows through Florence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arno is the river running through Florence, and a flower in crosswords is a river.

clue.text: Trainee working at country house travels a great distance

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a trainee driver's car
on means working, as a machine
a grange is a country house with farm buildings

explanation.surface: An apprentice employed at a manor travels far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something described as long-range is able to cover great distances, like a long-range missile.

clue.text: Suspect might be losing a game

parts.note: rum means odd or suspect

indicators.note: losing signals that the letter a drops out

parts.note: may means might

explanation.surface: A suspect might be losing at cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' looks like a noun for an accused person, but it is the adjective meaning dubious or odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rummy is a card game of collecting sets and runs.

clue.text: Search for Pole cut short — frightened noise interrupts

indicators.note: interrupts means the noise breaks into the shortened word
cut short means the last letter is removed

parts.note: the South Pole
eek is a frightened squeal

explanation.surface: A Polish man is cut off by a startled cry while searching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' wants to be a Polish person; it is one of the Earth's poles, shortened by 'cut short', with 'interrupts' breaking in the cry.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek out is to search for and find someone or something.

clue.text: One held socks with label inside

indicators.note: inside places the label within the hosiery

parts.note: hose are socks or stockings
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A sock with its label inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One held' reads as a passive aside, but it names a captive.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person held captive as security.
